title: Move to the wall
brief:
Karel is a robot. Karel understands a few commands, and each command is a function you call.

Karel is at the left end of a corridor, facing east. Move Karel to the far end, right up against the wall.

Write your commands inside main(). One move() moves Karel one square. Count the squares!

vocabulary.gloss: a named piece of code you can run by writing its name with brackets, like move()
to run a function: move() calls the function move
commands run one after another, in the order you write them
the function where your program starts

hints: Each move() moves Karel exactly one square. Karel starts on square 1 and the wall is after square 6.
Karel needs to move 5 times: from square 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 4, 4 to 5, and 5 to 6.
Write move() five times inside main(), each on its own line, all indented by 4 spaces.
solution:
def main():
    move()
    move()
    move()
    move()
    move()
